title: Impact of Institutional Ownership on Firm Value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV / Two-Stage Least Squares)**

**Rationale:** The research question asks whether institutional ownership (x) causally affects firm value (y). OLS estimation of this relationship is likely biased due to endogeneity: institutional investors may select firms based on unobservable characteristics correlated with firm value (e.g., growth prospects, governance quality), creating reverse causality and omitted variable bias.

**Instrument:** S&P 500 index inclusion (z) serves as an instrument for institutional ownership (x). Index inclusion mechanically increases institutional ownership because index funds and ETFs must hold constituent stocks, providing exogenous variation in ownership structure.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **Relevance:** S&P 500 inclusion significantly predicts institutional ownership (strong first stage). We test this with the first-stage F-statistic.
2. **Exclusion Restriction:** Index inclusion affects firm value *only* through its effect on institutional ownership, not through other channels (e.g., direct prestige effects, liquidity changes). This is the identifying assumption — it is not directly testable but is standard in this literature.
3. **Independence:** Index inclusion is as-good-as-random conditional on controls (no selection on unobservables correlated with firm value beyond what flows through institutional ownership).

## 2. R Code

```r
# ============================================================
# IV Analysis: Impact of Institutional Ownership on Firm Value
# ============================================================

library(AER)       # ivreg for 2SLS
library(lmtest)    # coeftest
library(sandwich)  # robust standard errors

# ---------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# ---------------------------
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s80_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(data), "x", ncol(data), "\n\n")
summary(data)
cat("\nCorrelation matrix:\n")
print(round(cor(data), 4))

# ---------------------------
# 2. OLS Baseline (Naive)
# ---------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("OLS ESTIMATION (Naive / Potentially Biased)\n")
cat("========================================\n")
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
print(summary(ols_model))

# OLS with robust SEs
cat("OLS with robust standard errors:\n")
print(coeftest(ols_model, vcov = vcovHC(ols_model, type = "HC1")))

# ---------------------------
# 3. First Stage: z -> x
# ---------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("FIRST STAGE: Institutional Ownership ~ S&P 500 Inclusion\n")
cat("========================================\n")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print(summary(first_stage))

# First-stage F-statistic for instrument strength
fs_fstat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic
f_value <- fs_fstat[1]
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:", round(f_value, 2), "\n")
if (f_value > 10) {
  cat("=> Instrument is STRONG (F > 10, Staiger-Stock rule of thumb)\n")
} else {
  cat("=> WARNING: Instrument may be WEAK (F < 10)\n")
}

# ---------------------------
# 4. Reduced Form: z -> y
# ---------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("REDUCED FORM: Firm Value ~ S&P 500 Inclusion\n")
cat("========================================\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Wald estimator (reduced form / first stage)
rf_coef <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
fs_coef <- coef(first_stage)["z"]
wald_estimate <- rf_coef / fs_coef
cat("\nWald (IV) estimate (reduced form coef / first stage coef):", 
    round(wald_estimate, 4), "\n")

# ---------------------------
# 5. IV / 2SLS Estimation
# ---------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("2SLS IV ESTIMATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
iv_summary <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
print(iv_summary)

# IV with robust standard errors
cat("\n2SLS with robust standard errors:\n")
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv_model, vcov = vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1"))
print(iv_robust)

# ---------------------------
# 6. Key Results Summary
# ---------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY OF KEY RESULTS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

ols_coef <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
ols_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(ols_model, type = "HC1")["x", "x"])
iv_coef <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1")["x", "x"])

cat(sprintf("OLS estimate of x on y:  %.4f (robust SE: %.4f)\n", ols_coef, ols_se))
cat(sprintf("IV  estimate of x on y:  %.4f (robust SE: %.4f)\n", iv_coef, iv_se))
cat(sprintf("First-stage F-statistic: %.2f\n", f_value))
cat(sprintf("Wald estimate:           %.4f\n", wald_estimate))

cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
if (iv_coef < 0) {
  cat(sprintf("A one-unit increase in institutional ownership DECREASES firm value by %.4f units.\n", abs(iv_coef)))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("A one-unit increase in institutional ownership INCREASES firm value by %.4f units.\n", iv_coef))
}

# ---------------------------
# 7. Robustness Checks
# ---------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# (a) Hausman test: Compare OLS vs IV
cat("\n--- (a) Hausman-type Endogeneity Test ---\n")
# Manual Hausman: add first-stage residuals to OLS
data$fs_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + controls + fs_resid, data = data)
hausman_pval <- summary(hausman_reg)$coefficients["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("P-value on first-stage residual in augmented regression:", 
    round(hausman_pval, 4), "\n")
if (hausman_pval < 0.05) {
  cat("=> Reject exogeneity of x at 5% level. IV is preferred over OLS.\n")
} else {
  cat("=> Cannot reject exogeneity of x. OLS may be consistent.\n")
}

# (b) IV without controls
cat("\n--- (b) IV without controls ---\n")
iv_nocontrols <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
print(summary(iv_nocontrols))
cat(sprintf("IV coefficient (no controls): %.4f\n", coef(iv_nocontrols)["x"]))

# (c) Anderson-Rubin confidence set (robust to weak instruments)
cat("\n--- (c) Anderson-Rubin Test (Robust to Weak IV) ---\n")
# Under H0: beta = 0, test reduced form coefficient on z
ar_test <- linearHypothesis(reduced_form, "z = 0")
cat("Anderson-Rubin F-stat:", round(ar_test$F[2], 4), 
    ", p-value:", round(ar_test$`Pr(>F)`[2], 4), "\n")

# (d) Sensitivity: exclude outliers
cat("\n--- (d) Excluding outliers (|y| > 3 or |x| > 3) ---\n")
data_trimmed <- data[abs(data$y) < 3 & abs(data$x) < 3, ]
cat("Observations after trimming:", nrow(data_trimmed), "\n")
if (nrow(data_trimmed) > 50) {
  iv_trimmed <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data_trimmed)
  cat(sprintf("IV coefficient (trimmed): %.4f (SE: %.4f)\n", 
              coef(iv_trimmed)["x"],
              summary(iv_trimmed)$coefficients["x", "Std. Error"]))
}

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("ANALYSIS COMPLETE\n")
cat("========================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign:** The IV estimate of institutional ownership on firm value is expected to be **negative**, consistent with the research hypothesis that increased institutional ownership (driven by index inclusion) negatively affects firm value.

**Magnitude:** Given the standardized-looking data (variables appear roughly mean-zero with moderate variance), I expect the IV coefficient to be in the range of approximately **-0.5 to -2.0**, though this depends heavily on the data-generating process. The IV estimate is likely to be larger in absolute value than the OLS estimate if OLS is biased toward zero (e.g., due to institutional investors selecting undervalued firms, creating positive bias that attenuates the negative causal effect).

**First Stage:** I expect a positive and significant first-stage coefficient (F > 10), indicating that S&P 500 inclusion significantly increases institutional ownership — this is well-established empirically.

**Hausman Test:** I anticipate rejecting the null of exogeneity, confirming that endogeneity is present and IV estimation is warranted.

**Economic Rationale for Negative Effect:** Possible channels include (1) excessive monitoring/short-termism pressures from index-tracking institutions, (2) reduced managerial discretion, (3) passive ownership reducing governance quality, or (4) crowding out of active, informed investors. However, this is a contested finding — much of the literature finds positive or null effects, so the negative result may reflect the specific DGP of this simulation.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use S&P 500 inclusion as an instrument for institutional ownership.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased institutional ownership, driven by index inclusion, leads to a decrease in firm value.
